fields.mechanism: Entropy generation analysis (EGA) within the framework of non-equilibrium thermodynamics to minimize total entropy generation rate in turbulent reacting flows.
fields.intervention: Integrate numerical modeling of the entropy transport equations using Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes to optimize the combustion chamber geometry and wall bounding conditions. This aims to minimize the lumped total entropy generation rate by reducing viscous dissipation and thermal diffusion gradients in the near-wall regions.
fields.expected_effect: Reduced thermodynamic losses due to irreversibilities, thereby improving the thermal conversion efficiency of the internal combustion engine.
fields.falsification_test: Perform a comparative entropy generation analysis on the baseline engine versus the optimized geometry; failure is defined if the total entropy generation rate in the optimized case is not lower than the baseline despite reduced predicted heat loss.
fields.mechanism_source_span: numerical modeling approaches are described within the continuum formulation

fields.mechanism: Entropy generation analysis in turbulent combustion systems to identify and minimize thermodynamic irreversibilities
fields.intervention: Apply entropy transport equations within Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes modeling to map local entropy production sources in the engine cylinder, then redesign combustion chamber geometry and injection timing to minimize identified entropy generation zones
fields.expected_effect: Reduction of total entropy generation rate during combustion, increasing maximum thermal conversion efficiency of the internal combustion engine
fields.falsification_test: Measure brake thermal efficiency before and after implementing EGA-guided geometric modifications on a single-cylinder test engine at constant load and speed; if efficiency does not increase by a statistically significant margin, the intervention fails
fields.mechanism_source_span: entropy generation analysis (EGA) in turbulent combustion systems. We account for various parametric studies
